united-arab-emirates.overview:
The United Arab Emirates packs more into a short trip than almost anywhere else in the world. Dubai delivers record-breaking towers, golden souks and desert safaris; Abu Dhabi adds the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Louvre Abu Dhabi and Yas Island; and the northern emirates bring quieter beaches and mountain views.

It is one of the easiest international trips from India: flights take about four hours, the weather is dependable through winter, and hotels, transfers and attractions are well organised for families, couples and groups. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.flight_time: About 3 hr 30 min to 4 hr from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Skyline and spectacle
reasons.text: Burj Khalifa, Dubai Frame, Palm Jumeirah and the Dubai Fountain make for a trip full of landmarks you will recognise.

reasons.title: Desert adventures
reasons.text: Dune bashing, camel rides, a barbecue dinner under the stars and a falconry show are all part of a classic evening safari.

reasons.title: Shopping and dining
reasons.text: From gold and spice souks to giant malls, and menus that cover everything from Indian vegetarian to fine dining.

reasons.title: Easy, safe and family friendly
reasons.text: Short flights, reliable infrastructure, very low crime and plenty of attractions for children and grandparents alike.

attractions.title: Burj Khalifa
attractions.text: The world's tallest building. The At The Top observation decks give sweeping views over the city and the Gulf.

attractions.title: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Abu Dhabi
attractions.text: A white-marble masterpiece with 82 domes and one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world.

attractions.title: Palm Jumeirah and Atlantis
attractions.text: The palm-shaped island is home to Atlantis, beach clubs and the Palm Jumeirah monorail.

attractions.title: Dubai Creek and the old souks
attractions.text: Cross the creek by abra boat and bargain for gold, textiles and spices in the Deira and Bur Dubai markets.

attractions.title: Museum of the Future
attractions.text: A striking calligraphy-covered building with immersive exhibits about technology and tomorrow.

attractions.title: Ferrari World and Yas Island
attractions.text: Theme parks, the Formula 1 circuit and waterparks make Yas Island a favourite with families.

experiences.title: Desert safari
experiences.text: A sunset drive over the dunes followed by a camp dinner, live entertainment and henna art.

experiences.title: Dhow cruise dinner
experiences.text: Glide along Dubai Marina or the Creek on a traditional wooden dhow with a buffet dinner on board.

experiences.title: Skydive and water sports
experiences.text: Jet-ski, parasail or take the plunge over the Palm for a once-in-a-lifetime view.

experiences.title: Hot air balloon at dawn
experiences.text: Float over the desert at sunrise, followed by breakfast in a Bedouin-style camp.

experiences.title: Mall hopping and Global Village
experiences.text: Spend a day at Dubai Mall or Mall of the Emirates, or visit Global Village in winter for pavilions from around the world.

food.title: Shawarma and falafel
food.text: Cheap, filling street food found on almost every corner.

food.title: Machboos and Emirati grills
food.text: Spiced rice with slow-cooked meat, best tried at a heritage restaurant in Al Fahidi.

food.title: Karak chai and dates
food.text: Strong, sweet tea with a plate of fresh dates at any local café.

food.title: Indian and Pakistani cuisine
food.text: Dubai has some of the best Indian restaurants outside India, including plenty of vegetarian and Jain options.

tips.title: Dress respectfully at religious sites
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees and carry a scarf for the Grand Mosque. Beach and pool wear is fine at resorts.

tips.title: Book big attractions early
tips.text: Burj Khalifa sunset slots and desert safaris sell out in peak winter weeks, so we book these ahead for you.

tips.title: Alcohol is only served in licensed venues
tips.text: Public drinking and intoxication are not allowed. Stick to hotels and licensed restaurants.

tips.title: Carry light layers
tips.text: Malls and metro cars are strongly air-conditioned even in the heat.

tips.title: Avoid midday heat in summer
tips.text: Plan outdoor activities for early morning and evening between May and September.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders need a UAE visa, normally issued online within a few working days. We collect your documents and apply on your behalf. Processing times and rules change, so we confirm the latest requirements at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations for travellers from India. Carry regular medicines with a prescription, drink plenty of water and use sunscreen. Tap water is safe, but most visitors prefer bottled water.
travel_info.money: Cards are accepted almost everywhere and AED is pegged to the US dollar. Tipping of 10 to 15 per cent is common in restaurants if no service charge is added. Indian rupees are not widely accepted, so exchange before you travel or withdraw at airport ATMs.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for the UAE?
faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Dubai and a day trip to Abu Dhabi comfortably. Add two more nights if you want a relaxed pace or a visit to Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah.

faqs.q: Is the UAE safe for families and solo women?
faqs.a: Yes. It is consistently ranked among the safest destinations in the world, and public transport and taxis are reliable at all hours.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: October to March is the peak season, with pleasant 20 to 30 degree days. May to September is very hot but hotels and flights are noticeably cheaper.

faqs.q: Do I need to book attractions in advance?
faqs.a: For Burj Khalifa, desert safaris and theme parks, yes. We can pre-book all of these for you so you never queue for tickets.

singapore.overview:
Singapore is a compact city-state where gleaming skylines, lush gardens and a dozen food cultures sit within a short ride of each other. In one trip you can walk through the Gardens by the Bay supertrees, cross to Sentosa for beaches and theme parks, eat your way through Little India and Chinatown, and spot pandas and white tigers on a night safari.

It is spotless, safe and extremely easy to get around, which makes it a favourite first international holiday for Indian families and a popular add-on to Malaysia and Indonesia. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.time_zone: UTC+8 (2 hr 30 min ahead of IST)
facts.climate: 25°C to 32°C all year, with frequent showers
facts.flight_time: About 5 to 6 hours from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Tamil is an official language
reasons.text: Signage, announcements and food are familiar to many Indian travellers, which makes the city feel welcoming from day one.

reasons.title: Something for every age
reasons.text: Universal Studios, S.E.A. Aquarium, Night Safari and Gardens by the Bay are all within easy reach of each other.

reasons.title: Brilliant public transport
reasons.text: A clean, air-conditioned MRT reaches almost every attraction, so you rarely lose time in traffic.

reasons.title: World-class food at hawker prices
reasons.text: Michelin-recognised street stalls serve full meals for a few dollars.

attractions.title: Gardens by the Bay
attractions.text: The Supertree Grove, Cloud Forest and Flower Dome are spectacular, especially at the evening light and sound show.

attractions.title: Marina Bay Sands and SkyPark
attractions.text: The most photographed building in the city, with an observation deck and views over the harbour.

attractions.title: Sentosa Island
attractions.text: Beaches, Universal Studios Singapore, cable car rides and the Wings of Time show.

attractions.title: Night Safari and River Wonders
attractions.text: The world's first nocturnal zoo, next to the river-themed wildlife park.

attractions.title: Little India and Chinatown
attractions.text: Colourful streets, temples, markets and some of the best food in the city.

attractions.title: Merlion Park and Clarke Quay
attractions.text: The national icon by day, and a lively riverside dining scene by night.

experiences.title: Universal Studios Singapore
experiences.text: Seven themed zones with rides for thrill-seekers and little ones alike.

experiences.title: Singapore River cruise
experiences.text: A relaxed bumboat ride past the old shophouses and the downtown skyline.

experiences.title: Cable car and luge on Sentosa
experiences.text: Fly across the harbour and race down the hill on a luge cart.

experiences.title: Orchard Road shopping
experiences.text: A kilometre of malls with global brands, electronics and seasonal sales.

experiences.title: Spectra light show
experiences.text: A free evening light and water show on the Marina Bay waterfront.

food.title: Hainanese chicken rice
food.text: The unofficial national dish, served at nearly every hawker centre.

food.title: Chilli crab
food.text: Sweet, spicy crab best eaten with fried mantou buns.

food.title: Laksa and kaya toast
food.text: A coconut noodle soup and a classic breakfast of toast with coconut jam.

food.title: Vegetarian and Indian food
food.text: Banana-leaf rice and dosa in Little India, and vegetarian stalls across the city.

tips.title: Strict rules on litter and chewing gum
tips.text: Fines are real, so bin everything and do not bring gum into the country.

tips.title: Carry an umbrella
tips.text: Short tropical showers are likely any day of the year.

tips.title: Get an EZ-Link or tap-and-pay card
tips.text: Public transport accepts contactless cards, which saves buying tickets each time.

tips.title: Dress light but cover up in temples
tips.text: Remove shoes and cover shoulders and knees at places of worship.

tips.title: Plan Sentosa and Universal on a weekday
tips.text: Queues are noticeably shorter outside weekends and school holidays.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders need a visa for Singapore, which is applied for online through an authorised agent. We prepare and submit the application for you. Requirements and processing times change, so we confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccines for travellers from India. Tap water is safe to drink. Carry mosquito repellent as dengue is present in the region.
travel_info.money: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere. Hawker centres sometimes prefer cash. A 10 per cent service charge plus tax is usually added at restaurants, so tipping is not expected.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Singapore?
faqs.a: Four nights is enough to cover the main attractions. Add a night or two if you want a day at Universal Studios or to combine it with Malaysia.

faqs.q: Is Singapore expensive?
faqs.a: Hotels and shopping are pricey, but street food, transport and many attractions are good value. We can include most of the big-ticket items in your package so your daily spend is limited to meals and shopping.

faqs.q: Can I combine Singapore with Malaysia or Bali?
faqs.a: Yes. Singapore pairs very well with Kuala Lumpur and Bali, and we offer combined itineraries on the packages below.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: Singapore is warm and humid all year. February to April is usually driest, while November to January brings the heaviest rain but also the festive lights.

malaysia.overview:
Malaysia is Southeast Asia's easiest all-rounder: modern cities, rainforest, beaches, hill stations and a food scene that blends Malay, Chinese and Indian flavours. Kuala Lumpur gives you the Petronas Twin Towers and Batu Caves, Genting adds cool mountain air and theme parks, and Langkawi offers quiet beaches and duty-free shopping.

Because English is widely spoken and Indian food is everywhere, it is a comfortable choice for first-time international travellers and multi-generation families. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.time_zone: UTC+8 (2 hr 30 min ahead of IST)
facts.flight_time: About 4 hr 30 min to 5 hr 30 min from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Great value
reasons.text: Hotels, food and attractions cost noticeably less than in Singapore or Dubai.

reasons.title: Something different every day
reasons.text: City towers one day, tea plantations and cable cars the next, and a beach the day after.

reasons.title: Familiar food
reasons.text: Banana-leaf meals, roti canai and vegetarian restaurants are easy to find, especially in Brickfields.

reasons.title: Easy to combine
reasons.text: Malaysia links naturally with Singapore, Thailand and Bali on one itinerary.

attractions.title: Petronas Twin Towers and KLCC Park
attractions.text: The skybridge and observation deck offer an unforgettable view, and the park below is a lovely evening stroll.

attractions.title: Batu Caves
attractions.text: A limestone cave temple reached by 272 rainbow-coloured steps, guarded by a giant golden statue of Lord Murugan.

attractions.title: Genting Highlands
attractions.text: A cool hill resort reached by cable car, with theme parks and entertainment.

attractions.title: Langkawi Sky Bridge and cable car
attractions.text: A curved suspension bridge high above the rainforest, with views to Thailand on clear days.

attractions.title: Putrajaya and the Pink Mosque
attractions.text: The planned government city with wide boulevards, lakes and striking Islamic architecture.

attractions.title: Melaka heritage town
attractions.text: A UNESCO-listed old town with colonial buildings, canal cruises and a vibrant night market.

experiences.title: Genting SkyWorlds and cable car
experiences.text: A gondola ride through the clouds to a hilltop theme park.

experiences.title: Langkawi island hopping
experiences.text: Boat trips to Pregnant Maiden Lake and eagle-feeding spots.

experiences.title: Kuala Lumpur food walk
experiences.text: Taste satay, nasi lemak and cendol along Jalan Alor and Petaling Street.

experiences.title: Cameron Highlands tea estates
experiences.text: Walk through tea plantations and strawberry farms in a cool mountain climate.

experiences.title: KL Tower and Aquaria
experiences.text: Skyline views from the tower, and an underwater tunnel at KLCC.

food.title: Nasi lemak
food.text: Coconut rice with sambal, peanuts and egg, the national breakfast.

food.title: Roti canai and teh tarik
food.text: Flaky flatbread with dhal curry, paired with frothy pulled tea.

food.title: Satay and laksa
food.text: Grilled skewers with peanut sauce, and a rich spicy noodle soup.

food.title: Vegetarian options
food.text: Brickfields and Little India in Kuala Lumpur are full of vegetarian restaurants serving South Indian meals.

tips.title: Check the arrival card
tips.text: Travellers are required to submit the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online before arrival.

tips.title: Dress modestly at temples and mosques
tips.text: Scarves and robes are lent at major sites such as the National Mosque.

tips.title: Genting weather changes quickly
tips.text: Carry a light jacket as temperatures drop and fog is common.

tips.title: Use Grab for taxis
tips.text: Ride-hailing is cheaper and more transparent than street taxis in Kuala Lumpur.

tips.title: Plan around the rain
tips.text: Afternoon showers are common, so schedule outdoor sightseeing in the morning.

travel_info.visa: Malaysia has offered visa-free entry for Indian passport holders for short tourist stays, together with the online MDAC arrival card. This arrangement has been extended in the past, so we verify the current rule before you travel.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Use mosquito repellent, especially in forested areas and on the islands. Bottled water is recommended.
travel_info.money: Cards are widely accepted in cities; keep cash for markets, small cafés and island trips. Tipping is optional, and many restaurants add a 6 per cent service tax and 10 per cent service charge.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Malaysia?
faqs.a: Five nights covers Kuala Lumpur, Genting and a few days on Langkawi. Add Singapore for a classic multi-country trip.

faqs.q: Is Malaysia good for vegetarians?
faqs.a: Yes, especially in Kuala Lumpur and Penang, where South Indian vegetarian restaurants are everywhere.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: The west coast, including Kuala Lumpur and Langkawi, is best from December to February. Showers are possible all year.

faqs.q: Can I take my family and elderly parents?
faqs.a: Absolutely. We can plan comfortable private transfers and moderate walking, and adjust the pace to suit older travellers.

indonesia.overview:
Indonesia stretches across more than 17,000 islands, and for most Indian travellers the story begins and ends with Bali. The Island of the Gods blends sacred temples, volcanic landscapes, terraced rice fields, surf beaches and some of the most welcoming people in Asia. Beyond Bali, Nusa Penida, the Gili Islands, Lombok and Komodo add dramatic cliffs and wildlife.

It is a natural honeymoon and friends' destination and increasingly popular with families. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.languages: Indonesian, Balinese, English in tourist areas
facts.time_zone: UTC+8 in Bali (2 hr 30 min ahead of IST)
facts.flight_time: About 7 to 9 hours, usually with one stop

reasons.title: Culture and nature together
reasons.text: Temple ceremonies, dance, volcanoes and rice terraces are all within a short drive of each other.

reasons.title: Honeymoon favourite
reasons.text: Private pool villas, candlelit dinners and spa days are very affordable in Bali.

reasons.title: Adventure on tap
reasons.text: Surf, snorkel, white-water raft, trek a volcano at sunrise or swing over a jungle valley.

reasons.title: Excellent value
reasons.text: Luxury villas and spas cost a fraction of equivalent stays in the Maldives or Europe.

attractions.title: Tanah Lot Temple
attractions.text: A sea temple perched on a rock offshore, especially photogenic at sunset.

attractions.title: Ubud and the Tegallalang rice terraces
attractions.text: Art galleries, yoga studios, the Monkey Forest and layers of green paddy fields.

attractions.title: Uluwatu Temple and Kecak dance
attractions.text: Clifftop temple and the sunset fire-dance performance.

attractions.title: Mount Batur and Kintamani
attractions.text: A sunrise trek or a scenic drive to a caldera lake and active volcano.

attractions.title: Nusa Penida
attractions.text: Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong and Broken Beach are among Indonesia's most dramatic coastlines.

attractions.title: Seminyak and Kuta beaches
attractions.text: Sunset beach clubs, surf lessons and nightlife.

experiences.title: Bali swing and jungle swing
experiences.text: Swing out over a jungle valley or rice terrace for dramatic photographs.

experiences.title: Water sports at Tanjung Benoa
experiences.text: Parasailing, banana boat, jet-ski and snorkelling in calm waters.

experiences.title: Sunrise volcano trek
experiences.text: A guided climb of Mount Batur with breakfast cooked by volcanic steam.

experiences.title: White-water rafting on the Ayung River
experiences.text: A family-friendly adventure through jungle gorges.

experiences.title: Balinese spa and cooking class
experiences.text: A traditional massage, and a hands-on lesson in local cooking.

food.title: Nasi goreng and mie goreng
food.text: Fried rice and noodles, available everywhere from street carts to resorts.

food.title: Satay lilit and bebek betutu
food.text: Balinese specialities worth trying at a local warung.

food.title: Fresh tropical fruit
food.text: Mango, mangosteen, papaya and dragon fruit at breakfast and in smoothie bowls.

food.title: Indian and vegetarian cafés
food.text: Bali has many vegetarian cafés and Indian restaurants, especially in Seminyak, Kuta and Ubud.

tips.title: Wear a sarong at temples
tips.text: A sarong and sash are required and are usually provided at the entrance.

tips.title: Hire a private driver
tips.text: Distances in Bali are slow because of traffic; a private car with driver is the easiest way to get around, and we can arrange it for you.

tips.title: Ride carefully
tips.text: Scooters are popular but accidents are common. We recommend a driver instead of renting a scooter.

tips.title: Mind the tourist levy
tips.text: Foreign visitors to Bali pay a one-time tourist levy on arrival, which is separate from the visa fee.

tips.title: Avoid the sea in the wet season
tips.text: Currents on the west coast can be strong. Swim only in patrolled areas.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders can get a visa on arrival in Bali, or apply for an e-VOA in advance. A one-time Bali tourist levy applies, and an arrival declaration form is required. Fees and rules change, so we confirm everything at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Drink only bottled or filtered water. Carry insect repellent, and be careful with ice and street food if you have a sensitive stomach.
travel_info.money: Cards work in resorts and larger restaurants. Carry rupiah for local warungs, taxis and markets. ATMs are widespread, but use machines inside banks or malls. A 10 per cent service charge plus tax is often added; tipping a few thousand rupiah is appreciated.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Bali?
faqs.a: Five to six nights is ideal for Ubud, Kintamani and the south coast. Add Nusa Penida or the Gili Islands with another two or three nights.

faqs.q: Is Bali good for honeymooners?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of our most popular honeymoon destinations, with private pool villas, candlelit dinners and couples spas included in many packages.

faqs.q: Is Bali safe for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The main tourist areas are very welcoming and family-friendly. We recommend a private driver and supervised water activities.

faqs.q: What is the best time to go?
faqs.a: April to October is dry and sunny. The wet season from November to March is cheaper and greener, with short, intense showers.

thailand.overview:
Thailand has something for every kind of traveller: golden temples and street food in Bangkok, limestone cliffs and turquoise bays in Phuket and Krabi, and the culture and cool air of Chiang Mai. It is warm, welcoming and good value, with a huge range of hotels, island resorts and activities.

It is one of the most popular international destinations for Indian families, friends and honeymooners. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.time_zone: UTC+7 (1 hr 30 min ahead of IST)
facts.climate: 25°C to 35°C; hot and humid, with monsoon showers from May to October
facts.flight_time: About 3 hr 30 min to 4 hr 30 min from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Beaches and islands
reasons.text: Phi Phi, Krabi and Phuket have some of Asia's most photogenic beaches and clear water.

reasons.title: City, culture and nightlife
reasons.text: Bangkok balances ornate temples and markets with rooftop bars, malls and the night scene.

reasons.title: Great value
reasons.text: Food, massages and day tours cost far less than in most Asian destinations.

reasons.title: Short flights
reasons.text: Direct flights from most Indian metros make it practical even for a long weekend.

attractions.title: Grand Palace and Wat Pho
attractions.text: Bangkok's glittering royal complex and the temple of the Reclining Buddha.

attractions.title: Phi Phi Islands
attractions.text: Maya Bay, Pileh Lagoon and Monkey Beach by speedboat from Phuket.

attractions.title: James Bond Island
attractions.text: Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts, best seen by longtail boat and sea canoe.

attractions.title: Coral Island, Pattaya
attractions.text: A short boat ride from Pattaya for parasailing, banana boats and glass-bottom boat rides.

attractions.title: Big Buddha and Wat Chalong, Phuket
attractions.text: A large hilltop Buddha with views over the island.

attractions.title: Chatuchak Market and Asiatique
attractions.text: Weekend shopping and an evening riverside market with a Ferris wheel.

experiences.title: Island hopping by speedboat
experiences.text: A full day visiting beaches, snorkelling spots and lagoons.

experiences.title: Thai massage and spa
experiences.text: A one-hour traditional massage, the most affordable luxury of the trip.

experiences.title: Alcazar or Tiffany cabaret show
experiences.text: A glamorous stage show that is popular with groups and families.

experiences.title: Safari World and Marine Park, Bangkok
experiences.text: An open zoo and marine show combined in one big day out.

experiences.title: Elephant sanctuary visit
experiences.text: Ethical sanctuaries where you can feed and walk beside rescued elephants without riding.

food.title: Pad Thai and green curry
food.text: Classics served fresh at street stalls and food courts.

food.title: Mango sticky rice
food.text: A dessert you will see everywhere and should try at least twice.

food.title: Som tam and tom yum
food.text: Spicy green papaya salad and hot-and-sour soup; ask for milder if you prefer.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Ask for 'jay' food, which is strictly vegetarian, or let us arrange Indian meal options.

tips.title: Dress properly in temples
tips.text: Shoulders and knees must be covered at the Grand Palace and other temples.

tips.title: Bargain at markets, not malls
tips.text: Politely negotiate at street markets; prices are fixed in shops.

tips.title: Respect the monarchy
tips.text: Avoid any disrespectful comment or gesture about the royal family.

tips.title: Check weather for island days
tips.text: Sea conditions can change between May and October, so boat tours may be rescheduled.

tips.title: Complete the digital arrival card
tips.text: Thailand requires an online Digital Arrival Card shortly before arrival.

travel_info.visa: Thailand has offered visa-free entry for Indian passport holders for short tourist stays, together with an online arrival card. Entry rules change often, so we confirm the current position and help you complete the arrival card.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Use sunscreen, stay hydrated and drink bottled water. Be careful on scooters and with sea currents in the monsoon.
travel_info.money: Carry Thai baht for markets and taxis, and use cards in hotels, malls and larger restaurants. ATMs charge a fee per withdrawal, so take out larger amounts less often. Tipping 20 to 50 baht is customary for good service.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Thailand?
faqs.a: Five to six nights covers Bangkok and Pattaya or Phuket. Seven to eight nights lets you add Krabi or Phi Phi at an easier pace.

faqs.q: Is Thailand good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Safari World, Coral Island, Phi Phi and the elephant sanctuaries are very popular with children.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: November to February is cool, dry and the busiest season. March to May is hot, and May to October is the monsoon, with lower prices.

faqs.q: Can I get Indian food easily?
faqs.a: Yes. Bangkok, Pattaya and Phuket have many Indian restaurants, and we can arrange Indian meals in your itinerary.

vietnam.overview:
Vietnam stretches along the coast of Southeast Asia, from the misty mountains of Sapa and the limestone seascape of Ha Long Bay in the north, to the lantern-lit streets of Hoi An and the beaches of Da Nang in the centre, to the energetic streets of Ho Chi Minh City in the south. It is a country of strong coffee, fresh herbs, motorbikes and warm hospitality.

For Indian travellers it is excellent value and increasingly well connected by direct flights. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.time_zone: UTC+7 (1 hr 30 min ahead of IST)
facts.flight_time: About 5 to 6 hours from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Dramatic landscapes
reasons.text: Ha Long Bay's limestone islands and the rice terraces of Sapa are among the most striking in Asia.

reasons.title: Charming old towns
reasons.text: Hoi An's lantern-lit streets and Hue's imperial citadel give the trip real character.

reasons.title: Remarkable food
reasons.text: Pho, banh mi and fresh spring rolls are excellent and very affordable.

reasons.title: Great value
reasons.text: Boutique hotels and day tours cost far less than in Thailand or Singapore.

attractions.title: Ha Long Bay
attractions.text: A UNESCO World Heritage seascape of limestone islands, best seen on a day or overnight cruise.

attractions.title: Golden Bridge, Ba Na Hills
attractions.text: A giant pair of stone hands lifting a golden bridge above the clouds.

attractions.title: Hoi An Ancient Town
attractions.text: A UNESCO-listed trading port of yellow shophouses, tailors and lanterns.

attractions.title: Hanoi Old Quarter
attractions.text: Thirty-six streets of markets, cafés, temples and the Hoan Kiem Lake.

attractions.title: Cu Chi Tunnels and Ho Chi Minh City
attractions.text: The underground network of the war era and a lively modern city.

attractions.title: Marble Mountains and My Khe Beach
attractions.text: Cave pagodas above Da Nang and one of Vietnam's best beaches.

experiences.title: Ha Long Bay cruise
experiences.text: Kayak through caves, taste seafood on deck and watch the sunset over the karsts.

experiences.title: Hoi An lantern evening
experiences.text: Float a paper lantern on the Thu Bon River and have clothes tailored in a day.

experiences.title: Mekong Delta day trip
experiences.text: Take a boat through canals and visit coconut candy workshops.

experiences.title: Motorbike and cyclo tours
experiences.text: A ride through Hanoi's Old Quarter with a local guide.

experiences.title: Vietnamese coffee workshop
experiences.text: Learn to make egg coffee and coconut coffee.

food.title: Pho
food.text: Aromatic noodle soup, traditionally eaten for breakfast.

food.title: Banh mi
food.text: A crusty baguette sandwich with herbs and pickles.

food.title: Cao lau and white rose dumplings
food.text: Hoi An specialities worth a stop.

food.title: Vegetarian dishes
food.text: Look for 'chay' restaurants, which are fully vegetarian, or let us arrange Indian meals.

tips.title: Cross the road slowly
tips.text: Walk at a steady pace and the motorbikes will go around you.

tips.title: Apply for the e-visa early
tips.text: Allow a few working days for the e-visa; we handle it with your package.

tips.title: Check the weather by region
tips.text: The north is cool and misty in winter, while the south is warm all year.

tips.title: Carry small notes
tips.text: Many small vendors do not take cards and cannot change big notes.

tips.title: Use Grab
tips.text: The ride-hailing app is cheap, reliable and avoids taxi disputes.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders can apply for a Vietnam e-visa online, which is valid for a single or multiple entries. We prepare the application, but processing times and fees change, so we confirm the latest at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Drink bottled water and be cautious with street food at first. Pack insect repellent and a light rain jacket.
travel_info.money: Dong is the local currency. Cards are accepted in hotels and larger restaurants; carry cash for markets and small shops. Tipping is not expected but 5 to 10 per cent is appreciated in tourist restaurants.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Six to seven nights covers Hanoi, Ha Long Bay and Da Nang with Hoi An. Eight or nine nights lets you add Ho Chi Minh City.

faqs.q: Is Vietnam safe for tourists?
faqs.a: Yes, it is generally very safe. Take normal care of bags in busy markets and cross roads carefully.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: December to May is a comfortable time for most regions. Typhoons are possible from August to October on the central coast.

faqs.q: Is Vietnam vegetarian friendly?
faqs.a: It can be, with some planning. Vegetarian restaurants are widely available in the cities, and we arrange Indian meal options where needed.

morocco.overview:
Morocco is a feast for the senses: the lantern-lit alleys of the Marrakech medina, the blue streets of Chefchaouen, the Sahara dunes at sunrise and the Atlas Mountains. Imperial cities such as Fez and Meknes preserve centuries of craft and architecture, while Casablanca and the Atlantic coast add a modern edge.

It is an adventurous but accessible choice for Indian travellers who have already done the Southeast Asia circuit. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.languages: Arabic, Berber, French; English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Hot summers, mild winters; cold nights in the desert and mountains
facts.flight_time: About 10 to 13 hours with one stop

reasons.title: Colour and craft
reasons.text: Souks sell leather, ceramics, carpets, lamps and spices, and artisans still work in front of you.

reasons.title: Desert and mountains
reasons.text: Camel treks and camp nights in the Sahara, and cool valleys in the Atlas Mountains.

reasons.title: Remarkable architecture
reasons.text: Riads, medinas, mosques and palaces covered in tile, carved plaster and cedar.

reasons.title: Unlike anywhere else
reasons.text: A mix of Arab, Berber, African and French influences gives the country a distinct character.

attractions.title: Jemaa el-Fnaa and Marrakech medina
attractions.text: A square that turns into a theatre of storytellers, food stalls and musicians at dusk.

attractions.title: Hassan II Mosque, Casablanca
attractions.text: One of the world's largest mosques, set on the Atlantic shore.

attractions.title: Fez el-Bali
attractions.text: The world's largest car-free urban area, with tanneries and ancient madrasas.

attractions.title: Chefchaouen
attractions.text: A mountain town painted in shades of blue.

attractions.title: Merzouga and the Sahara
attractions.text: Erg Chebbi dunes, camel treks and nights in a desert camp.

attractions.title: Ait Benhaddou
attractions.text: A fortified village used as a set for many films.

experiences.title: Camel trek and Sahara camp
experiences.text: Ride at sunset, dine by lantern and sleep under the stars.

experiences.title: Hot air balloon over Marrakech
experiences.text: A sunrise flight above the palm groves and the Atlas Mountains.

experiences.title: Cooking class in a riad
experiences.text: Learn to make tagine and Moroccan mint tea.

experiences.title: Hammam and spa
experiences.text: A traditional steam bath and scrub.

experiences.title: Souk shopping with a guide
experiences.text: Learn to bargain for rugs, leather, ceramics and spices.

food.title: Tagine
food.text: Slow-cooked stew with meat or vegetables, served in a clay pot.

food.title: Couscous on Fridays
food.text: The traditional weekly family meal, found in many restaurants.

food.title: Mint tea and pastries
food.text: Sweet green tea poured from a height and served with almond pastries.

food.title: Vegetarian options
food.text: Vegetable tagines, lentil soup and salads are easy to find; let us know your dietary needs in advance.

tips.title: Dress modestly
tips.text: Loose clothing that covers shoulders and knees is more comfortable and respectful, especially in the medinas.

tips.title: Agree prices first
tips.text: Settle the price before taking a taxi, a guide or a photograph with performers.

tips.title: Carry a light jacket
tips.text: Evenings in the desert and the mountains can be cold even in summer.

tips.title: Avoid tap water
tips.text: Drink bottled water and be cautious with raw salads.

tips.title: Plan around Ramadan
tips.text: Ramadan changes opening hours and restaurant availability, so check the dates when you plan your trip.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders need a visa for Morocco, and the process depends on your documents and travel history. We guide you through the application and confirm current requirements at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Bring any regular medicines, a stomach remedy, and sun protection for the desert.
travel_info.money: Moroccan dirham cannot be obtained outside Morocco in most cases, so withdraw or exchange on arrival. Cards are accepted in hotels and larger restaurants; carry cash for souks and taxis. Tipping 10 per cent is customary.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Morocco?
faqs.a: Eight to nine nights covers the imperial cities, the Sahara and Marrakech without rushing. A shorter trip can focus on Marrakech and the desert.

faqs.q: Is Morocco safe for Indian travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Visitors are generally welcomed warmly. Expect persistent sales approaches in the medinas, and agree on prices first.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: April to June and September to November are comfortable. Summers are very hot inland, and winters are cold in the mountains.

faqs.q: Can I get vegetarian food?
faqs.a: Yes, vegetable tagines, couscous, soups and salads are common. We help with arrangements ahead of time.

azerbaijan.overview:
Azerbaijan, the Land of Fire, sits where Europe meets Asia on the shore of the Caspian Sea. Baku mixes a walled old city with flame-shaped skyscrapers and a lively boulevard, while day trips lead to mud volcanoes, fire temples and Caucasus villages such as Gabala and Sheki.

It is short-haul, affordable and visa-friendly for Indians, which has made it one of the fastest-growing destinations in the region. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.languages: Azerbaijani, Russian, English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Warm summers, mild winters; cooler in the mountains
facts.flight_time: About 5 to 6 hours from major Indian cities

reasons.title: Where old meets futuristic
reasons.text: The Flame Towers and Heydar Aliyev Centre sit beside a UNESCO-listed old city.

reasons.title: Caucasus scenery
reasons.text: Cable cars, waterfalls and mountain villages in Gabala and Shahdag.

reasons.title: Simple e-visa
reasons.text: Indian travellers can apply for an e-visa online.

reasons.title: Good value
reasons.text: Hotels, food and transport are affordable, with easy day trips from Baku.

attractions.title: Icheri Sheher, Baku Old City
attractions.text: A walled medieval city with the Maiden Tower and Palace of the Shirvanshahs.

attractions.title: Flame Towers
attractions.text: Three skyscrapers that light up as flames after dark.

attractions.title: Heydar Aliyev Centre
attractions.text: A flowing white building designed by Zaha Hadid.

attractions.title: Gobustan and the mud volcanoes
attractions.text: Ancient rock carvings and bubbling mud craters.

attractions.title: Ateshgah Fire Temple and Yanar Dag
attractions.text: Sites linked to the country's fire-worshipping heritage, with a hillside that burns continuously.

attractions.title: Gabala and Shamakhi
attractions.text: Mountain resorts, waterfalls and cable cars in the Caucasus foothills.

experiences.title: Baku Boulevard walk and Caspian views
experiences.text: A seaside promenade with parks, fountains and cafés.

experiences.title: Gabala cable car and Tufandag
experiences.text: Mountain rides with views of the Caucasus.

experiences.title: Sheki caravanserai and khan's palace
experiences.text: Silk Road architecture and traditional halva.

experiences.title: Tea house experience
experiences.text: Sit in a traditional tea house with a samovar and jam.

experiences.title: Baku night walk
experiences.text: The lit-up Old City and Fountain Square at night.

food.title: Plov
food.text: Saffron rice with lamb or chicken, the national dish.

food.title: Dolma and qutab
food.text: Stuffed vine leaves, and thin pancakes filled with greens or meat.

food.title: Azerbaijani tea
food.text: Served in pear-shaped glasses with sugar cubes or jam.

food.title: Vegetarian choices
food.text: Eggplant dishes, lentil soup, qutabs with greens and salads are widely available.

tips.title: Apply for the e-visa early
tips.text: Allow a few working days for approval.

tips.title: Baku is windy
tips.text: Carry a light jacket even in warmer months.

tips.title: Learn a few Russian or Azerbaijani words
tips.text: English is common in hotels, but not in smaller towns.

tips.title: Dress respectfully at mosques
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf.

tips.title: Use Bolt or Yango
tips.text: Ride-hailing apps are cheap and reliable in Baku.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders can apply for an Azerbaijan e-visa online, normally approved within a few working days. We prepare and submit the application, and confirm current fees and rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Drink bottled water and carry any regular medication.
travel_info.money: Manat is the local currency, and cards are accepted in Baku. Carry cash for small towns and markets. A 10 per cent tip is customary where service is not included.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Azerbaijan?
faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Baku, Gabala and Sheki. Three nights is enough for Baku with a day trip.

faqs.q: Can I combine it with Georgia?
faqs.a: Yes. Many travellers pair Baku with Tbilisi on a combined Caucasus itinerary.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: April to June is pleasant. July and August are warm. Winters are mild in Baku and snowy in the mountains.

faqs.q: Is it good for couples and families?
faqs.a: Yes, it is comfortable for families, couples and groups, with an easy pace and good hotels.

georgia.overview:
Georgia is a small country with big landscapes: the Greater Caucasus rises above Kazbegi, vineyards stretch across Kakheti, and Tbilisi weaves together sulphur baths, cafés and old wooden balconies. Its alphabet, language and wine culture go back thousands of years, and its hospitality is famous.

It is a fast-growing choice for Indian travellers who enjoy scenery, food and easy road trips. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.languages: Georgian, Russian, English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Warm summers, cold snowy winters in the mountains
facts.flight_time: About 7 to 9 hours with one stop

reasons.title: Mountains within reach
reasons.text: Kazbegi and Gudauri are a few hours from Tbilisi by road.

reasons.title: Wine, food and hospitality
reasons.text: Cheese-filled breads, dumplings and 8,000-year-old winemaking traditions.

reasons.title: Compact and easy to travel
reasons.text: Short drives link the capital with mountains, vineyards and heritage towns.

reasons.title: Affordable
reasons.text: Good hotels and restaurants at modest prices.

attractions.title: Tbilisi Old Town and sulphur baths
attractions.text: Narrow streets, balconies and a Narikala fortress above the city.

attractions.title: Gergeti Trinity Church, Kazbegi
attractions.text: A mountaintop church beneath Mount Kazbek.

attractions.title: Gudauri and the Friendship Monument
attractions.text: A scenic ski resort and viewpoint on the Georgian Military Highway.

attractions.title: Mtskheta
attractions.text: The ancient capital with UNESCO-listed Svetitskhoveli Cathedral.

attractions.title: Kakheti wine region
attractions.text: Vineyards, monasteries and cellar tastings in the shadow of the Caucasus.

attractions.title: Batumi
attractions.text: A seaside city with a boulevard, botanical garden and Black Sea beaches.

experiences.title: Cable car to Narikala
experiences.text: Ride high above Tbilisi for views of the old town.

experiences.title: Wine tasting in Kakheti
experiences.text: Taste qvevri wine at a family cellar.

experiences.title: Georgian cooking class
experiences.text: Learn to fold khinkali and bake khachapuri.

experiences.title: Snow activities at Gudauri
experiences.text: Skiing, snowmobiles and paragliding in winter.

experiences.title: Jeep ride to Gergeti
experiences.text: A 4x4 ride up to the church with Caucasus views.

food.title: Khachapuri
food.text: Cheese-filled bread, often topped with an egg.

food.title: Khinkali
food.text: Large soup dumplings eaten by hand.

food.title: Georgian wine
food.text: Amber qvevri wines unique to the region.

food.title: Vegetarian dishes
food.text: Badrijani nigvzit (eggplant rolls), pkhali and lobio are naturally vegetarian.

tips.title: Check road conditions in winter
tips.text: Mountain roads to Kazbegi can close after snow.

tips.title: Carry cash in rural areas
tips.text: Cards work in cities but not always in villages.

tips.title: Dress for the altitude
tips.text: Nights are cold in the mountains even in summer.

tips.title: Cover up in churches
tips.text: Women are asked to cover their heads and legs; scarves are lent at the entrance.

tips.title: Book wine tours ahead
tips.text: Popular cellars get busy in autumn harvest.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders can apply for a Georgia e-visa online, and the process is simpler if you hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visa. We apply on your behalf and confirm current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Tap water is generally safe in Tbilisi, but many visitors prefer bottled water.
travel_info.money: Lari is the local currency. Cards are widely accepted in Tbilisi and Batumi. Tipping 10 per cent is customary in restaurants if service is not included.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Georgia?
faqs.a: Five to six nights covers Tbilisi, Kazbegi and Kakheti. Add two nights for Batumi.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: May to October is warm and good for hiking. December to March is best for snow and skiing.

faqs.q: Is Georgia safe for Indian travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgians are very welcoming. Take usual precautions with valuables in busy places.

faqs.q: Can I get vegetarian food?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgian cuisine has many vegetarian dishes, and we help with Indian meals where required.

kazakhstan.overview:
Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country, and its best-known highlights are close to Almaty: snow-capped Tian Shan peaks, turquoise Kolsai Lakes, Charyn Canyon and Big Almaty Lake. Astana adds a futuristic skyline of towers and domes, while Almaty offers cafés, bazaars and cable cars.

It is a refreshing, outdoorsy alternative to the usual beach circuit, with direct flights from Delhi and easy entry rules for Indian travellers. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

reasons.title: Big mountains close to the city
reasons.text: Shymbulak and Medeu are a short drive from downtown Almaty.

reasons.title: Adventure scenery
reasons.text: Charyn Canyon, Kolsai Lakes and Kaindy Lake offer dramatic landscapes.

reasons.title: Short direct flight
reasons.text: About four hours from Delhi.

reasons.title: Far from the crowds
reasons.text: A rare chance to see wide landscapes without crowds.

attractions.title: Big Almaty Lake
attractions.text: A turquoise alpine lake at about 2,500 m, a short drive from the city.

attractions.title: Medeu and Shymbulak
attractions.text: An outdoor skating rink and a ski resort reached by a cable car.

attractions.title: Charyn Canyon
attractions.text: Red rock formations often compared to the Grand Canyon.

attractions.title: Kolsai and Kaindy Lakes
attractions.text: Alpine lakes on forested mountain slopes, and a sunken forest.

attractions.title: Kok Tobe Hill
attractions.text: A viewpoint with a cable car, cafés and a small zoo.

attractions.title: Astana skyline
attractions.text: Bayterek Tower, Khan Shatyr and the Palace of Peace and Reconciliation.

experiences.title: Shymbulak cable car
experiences.text: A ride up to 3,200 m for snow views even in summer.

experiences.title: Horse riding and yurt stay
experiences.text: A taste of nomadic life with a local family.

experiences.title: Charyn Canyon walk
experiences.text: A guided walk through the Valley of Castles.

experiences.title: Green Bazaar tasting
experiences.text: Sample dried fruit, nuts and honey at Almaty's market.

experiences.title: Winter skiing and snowboarding
experiences.text: Shymbulak is a good, affordable ski resort.

food.title: Beshbarmak
food.text: Boiled meat over flat noodles, the national dish.

food.title: Baursak
food.text: Fried dough puffs eaten with tea.

food.title: Kumis
food.text: Fermented mare's milk, an acquired taste.

food.title: Vegetarian and Indian food
food.text: Almaty has Indian restaurants and cafés with vegetarian options.

tips.title: Layer your clothing
tips.text: Temperatures drop quickly with altitude, even in summer.

tips.title: Road trips take time
tips.text: Charyn and Kolsai are long drives, so start early.

tips.title: Carry cash for remote areas
tips.text: Cards are accepted in Almaty and Astana only.

tips.title: Check ski season dates
tips.text: Skiing normally runs from December to March.

tips.title: Book park permits through us
tips.text: Some national park areas need advance permits, which we arrange.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders have been able to enter Kazakhstan visa-free for short stays. Rules can change, so we verify the current position before you travel.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Carry warm clothing, sun protection and any regular medicines.
travel_info.money: Tenge is the local currency. Cards are widely accepted in Almaty and Astana. Tipping 10 per cent is customary in restaurants.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in Kazakhstan?
faqs.a: Five to six nights is ideal for Almaty with the lakes and Charyn Canyon. Add Astana for a longer trip.

faqs.q: What is the best time to go?
faqs.a: June to August is best for lakes and hiking. December to March is for skiing.

faqs.q: Is it good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, with easy-paced sightseeing in Almaty and a few longer road trips that can be skipped.

faqs.q: Can I combine Kazakhstan with Uzbekistan?
faqs.a: Yes, a Silk Road itinerary combining both is popular.

uzbekistan.overview:
Uzbekistan is the heart of the Silk Road, where turquoise-tiled domes, towering minarets and bustling bazaars rise from the desert. Samarkand's Registan Square, Bukhara's medieval old town and Khiva's walled city feel like open-air museums, while Tashkent adds Soviet-era grandeur and a modern metro.

It is a culture-first destination with direct flights from Delhi and growing numbers of Indian visitors. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

reasons.title: World-class architecture
reasons.text: Tilework and domes in Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva that rival anywhere in the world.

reasons.title: Authentic bazaars
reasons.text: Silk, ceramics and spices sold the way they have been for centuries.

reasons.title: Easy Silk Road touring
reasons.text: A fast train links Tashkent, Samarkand and Bukhara in a few hours.

reasons.title: Warm hospitality
reasons.text: Visitors are welcomed with tea, bread and plenty of curiosity.

attractions.title: Registan Square, Samarkand
attractions.text: Three madrasas facing a grand square, especially stunning at dusk.

attractions.title: Shah-i-Zinda
attractions.text: A street of blue-tiled mausoleums in Samarkand.

attractions.title: Lyabi-Hauz and Poi Kalyan, Bukhara
attractions.text: A historic pond and minaret in a living old town.

attractions.title: Itchan Kala, Khiva
attractions.text: A walled desert city of mud-brick and tilework.

attractions.title: Tashkent metro
attractions.text: Stations decorated like underground palaces.

attractions.title: Chorsu Bazaar
attractions.text: A domed market for dried fruit, spices and fresh bread.

experiences.title: High-speed Afrosiyob train
experiences.text: A comfortable ride between Tashkent, Samarkand and Bukhara.

experiences.title: Plov cooking class
experiences.text: Learn how Uzbek pilaf is cooked in a giant cauldron.

experiences.title: Silk and ceramics workshops
experiences.text: Visit artisans in Margilan and Gijduvan.

experiences.title: Old-town evening walk in Bukhara
experiences.text: The lit-up domes and caravanserais after sunset.

experiences.title: Folk dance and dinner
experiences.text: An evening of traditional music at a madrasa courtyard.

food.title: Plov
food.text: Rice with carrots and lamb, the national dish.

food.title: Samsa
food.text: Baked pastries filled with meat or pumpkin.

food.title: Fresh bread (non)
food.text: Round bread baked in clay ovens and stamped with patterns.

food.title: Vegetarian choices
food.text: Salads, lentil soup and vegetable samsa are available; we arrange Indian meals too.

tips.title: Dress modestly
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites.

tips.title: Carry cash
tips.text: Cards are accepted in major hotels but cash is common elsewhere.

tips.title: Visit in spring or autumn
tips.text: Summers are very hot and winters are cold.

tips.title: Ask before photographing people
tips.text: Most are happy to be photographed, but ask first.

tips.title: Book train tickets early
tips.text: Afrosiyob trains fill up quickly in season; we handle this.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders can apply for an Uzbekistan e-visa online. We submit it for you and confirm the latest rules and fees at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Drink bottled water and carry sun protection.
travel_info.money: Som is the local currency. Cards are accepted in hotels and larger restaurants, but cash is needed in bazaars. A small tip of 10 per cent is appreciated.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Uzbekistan?
faqs.a: Six to seven nights covers Tashkent, Samarkand and Bukhara, with Khiva added for longer trips.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: April to June and September to October have the best weather.

faqs.q: Is it good for older travellers?
faqs.a: Yes, with comfortable trains, short walks and good hotels, although summers are hot.

faqs.q: Can I get vegetarian food?
faqs.a: Yes, with salads, soups and bread. We also help arrange Indian meals.

tanzania.overview:
Tanzania pairs one of the world's great wildlife spectacles with white-sand beaches. The Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater deliver big cats, elephants and the Great Migration, while Zanzibar adds turquoise water, spice farms and the winding lanes of Stone Town.

It is a bucket-list trip for families and honeymooners who want adventure and relaxation in one holiday. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.capital: Dodoma (Dar es Salaam is the largest city)
facts.climate: Warm, with long rains March to May and short rains in November
facts.flight_time: About 10 to 12 hours with one stop

reasons.title: Wildlife at its best
reasons.text: Lions, leopards, elephants, giraffes and huge herds of wildebeest on the plains.

reasons.title: Safari and beach combined
reasons.text: Finish a game drive week with a few days of relaxation in Zanzibar.

reasons.title: Ngorongoro Crater
reasons.text: A natural amphitheatre with one of Africa's highest concentrations of wildlife.

reasons.title: Culture and spice
reasons.text: Meet Maasai communities and explore Stone Town's UNESCO-listed old streets.

attractions.title: Serengeti National Park
attractions.text: Endless plains with lions, cheetahs and, depending on the season, the Great Migration.

attractions.title: Ngorongoro Crater
attractions.text: A volcanic caldera with elephants, rhinos, hippos and lions.

attractions.title: Tarangire National Park
attractions.text: Famous for large elephant herds and giant baobab trees.

attractions.title: Lake Manyara
attractions.text: A soda lake with flamingos and tree-climbing lions.

attractions.title: Stone Town, Zanzibar
attractions.text: A UNESCO World Heritage old town with carved doors and bustling markets.

attractions.title: Nungwi and Kendwa beaches
attractions.text: Soft white sand and calm water on Zanzibar's north coast.

experiences.title: Game drives
experiences.text: Morning and late afternoon drives in open-roof 4x4 vehicles with an expert guide.

experiences.title: Hot air balloon safari
experiences.text: A sunrise flight above the Serengeti plains, followed by a bush breakfast.

experiences.title: Spice farm tour
experiences.text: Smell and taste cloves, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg on Zanzibar.

experiences.title: Sunset dhow cruise
experiences.text: A traditional sailing boat around Zanzibar with drinks and seafood.

experiences.title: Prison Island and Safari Blue
experiences.text: Giant tortoises, snorkelling and a seafood lunch on a sandbank.

food.title: Zanzibar pizza
food.text: A stuffed, pan-fried street snack found at Forodhani Gardens.

food.title: Pilau and biryani
food.text: Spiced rice dishes showing Indian and Arab influences.

food.title: Fresh seafood
food.text: Grilled fish, octopus and lobster on the coast.

food.title: Vegetarian and Indian food
food.text: Zanzibar has a long Indian community and many Indian restaurants, so vegetarian options are easy to find.

tips.title: Pack neutral clothes for safari
tips.text: Tan, olive and khaki are best, and avoid dark blue or black, which attract tsetse flies.

tips.title: Bring insect repellent and sunscreen
tips.text: Both are essential on safari and at the beach.

tips.title: Ask about malaria precautions
tips.text: Speak to your doctor about malaria prevention well before travel.

tips.title: Keep your distance from animals
tips.text: Stay inside the vehicle and follow your guide's instructions.

tips.title: Respect local dress codes in Zanzibar
tips.text: Cover up when walking in Stone Town, especially near mosques.

travel_info.visa: Indian passport holders need a visa for Tanzania, available online as an e-visa. We help prepare it and confirm the latest fees and rules at booking. Check yellow fever certificate requirements if you transit through a risk country.
travel_info.health: See your doctor 4 to 6 weeks before travel for advice on malaria prevention and vaccinations. Drink bottled water and use repellent.
travel_info.money: US dollars are widely accepted in parks and tourist hotels, and shillings are used locally. Cards work in larger hotels and lodges. Tipping your safari guide and camp staff is customary, and we advise on amounts.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Tanzania?
faqs.a: A week to ten days is ideal for a northern safari plus a few days on Zanzibar.

faqs.q: When is the best time for safari?
faqs.a: June to October is the dry season and the best for wildlife viewing. The Great Migration moves around the Serengeti during the year.

faqs.q: Is Tanzania safe for families?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with reputable lodges and guides. Some operators set minimum ages for game drives, which we check for you.

faqs.q: Can I add Zanzibar to a safari?
faqs.a: Yes. Many travellers finish a mainland safari with a few beach days in Zanzibar, and we can combine the two in one itinerary.
